one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this psychologist was quite mixed, and unfortunately, I ultimately didn’t feel that she was the right fit for me.

I first saw her last year. While she did provide professional information, strategies and homework, I personally found the approach quite clinical and scripted. After some appointments, I remember discussing the advice with my partner at the time and feeling that much of the information was something I could have researched or worked through myself. I was hoping for a deeper level of understanding and a more personalised approach.

Interestingly, I returned again this year without initially realising that I had previously seen the same psychologist. This time, I was going through a much more difficult period personally and my mental health was not in a great place. Because of that, I was looking for someone who could provide not only professional guidance, but also patience, empathy and a space where I genuinely felt heard.

I want to be fair and acknowledge that I did miss appointments, and I take responsibility for that. At the time, however, I was managing a lot personally and understood from discussions with my doctor that I could work through my available sessions at a pace that was manageable for me.

Unfortunately, a later phone conversation left me feeling uncomfortable with the way I was spoken to. I felt the interaction was more confrontational than supportive, particularly considering the circumstances in which I had originally sought psychological help. I chose to politely end the conversation and decided that it would be better for me to find another psychologist.

I don’t believe this necessarily means she would be the wrong psychologist for everyone. Different people respond to different therapeutic styles. For me personally, however, I needed a warmer, more individualised and emotionally supportive approach.

I respect the work psychologists do, but I also believe people seeking mental health support should feel comfortable, respected and heard. Unfortunately, that wasn’t consistently my experience here.

GT Insurance uses both intimidating, unacceptable, and inappropriate handling in their claims processes.

An accident on 09/04/2024 involving their insured driver resulted in my vehicle being written off, leaving me without a vehicle for 18 months and causing massive family disruption and loss of income.

On 10/07/2025, I received one of two demand letters from GT Insurance for the amount of $23,040.08, and another on 31/07/2025 as a final notice to pay for costs incurred by them for the loss of their insured vehicle. As if this was not completely unacceptable, on 01/09/2025, they sent Cox Commercial (a debt collector) to my home address to try to intimidate me for the above-mentioned amount.

This was where my 19-year-old son, who answered the door to this male debt collector, was told that the driver—my husband—had passed away in January 2025. When asked if the debt collector would like to speak to me, he rejected this offer and left. However, this experience caused my son added trauma at a time when he was already suffering from the loss of his father.

This below-ethical insurance company even went as far as to hire legal representation after I obtained legal assistance from Caxton Legal to protect myself against the false liability they were desperately trying to push onto me. From this point, GT Insurance went quiet until I contacted them on 17/07/2026 to pursue the cost of damages caused to me by their insured driver. I was met with a response of "We should both bear our own costs," to which I lodged a complaint with AFCA. Still, this dishonest company denies liability, maintains their dishonest position, and further extends my financial loss, damages, and severity by 29 months in total and counting every day.

Despite their insured driver's own admittance in the police report taking ownership of the accident, evidence at the scene clearly proving fault, and contact made by me to the police station that investigated this accident firmly naming GT Insurance's driver at fault, they still unbelievably maintain their position of not being at fault and that both parties should bear their own costs.

A revolting and dishonest insurance company, to say the very least. Imagine going above and beyond to bully and push an innocent family already in financial difficulty due to an accident caused by their insured driver, and acting so low and pathetic as to try to obtain money from people who are actually owed money by them. "Shameful" doesn't even begin to sum this company up.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely unacceptable service — left a quadriplegic passenger stranded in the Adelaide CBD for over 3 hours!!

Last night I was supporting my quadriplegic client in the Adelaide CBD when we suddenly discovered that the tyres on his power wheelchair had gone flat. We only needed to get him to an OTR so we could use a compression pump to get the tyres inflated enough to safely get him home.

Unfortunately, his accessible van was parked at a bus station which is locked overnight, meaning we could not access the vehicle. Access Cabs was our only realistic option.

We repeatedly attempted to book an Access Cab. We would receive a booking and tracking information, only for the booking to be cancelled without any proper notification. We continued trying again and again, and at other times we were simply told that there were no Access Cabs available.

We exhausted every other option. We contacted an ambulance, who advised they could transport my client but could not take his power wheelchair. We contacted police, who attended and attempted to manually pump the tyre, but unfortunately that was unsuccessful.

We eventually joined the RAA and had someone attend, only to be told that the tyre was actually punctured and required replacement. This meant that getting an accessible vehicle was our only option.

By this point, we had been stranded outside in the cold for approximately three hours.

We called Access Cabs AGAIN, only to eventually be told that there was ONE Access driver available and that the driver had refused to pick up my client because he was allegedly “dangerous.”

This was absolutely unacceptable.

My client does not even live in Adelaide and had never used an Access Cab here before, so we were completely unaware of any previous incident that could possibly justify such a statement. No explanation or evidence was provided to us, and the claim was completely inconsistent with our experience of the situation that night.

Up until that point, we had been extremely polite and patient with the staff on the phone despite the circumstances. However, being told that my disabled client was being refused transport because he was supposedly “dangerous” after leaving him stranded for hours was incredibly distressing and infuriating.

The staff member I spoke to was also extremely rude and dismissive about the situation rather than showing any understanding or urgency.

How can you advertise yourself as a 24/7 accessible transport service when a quadriplegic passenger can be left stranded in the city for hours with no accessible transport available?

After we reported the situation to police, police had to speak with Access Cabs directly. Only then were we told that a driver would be sent to us.

We waited another 20 minutes — and still nobody arrived.

At that point, we had absolutely no choice but to have my client drive his power wheelchair back to UCity where he was staying, despite the risk of causing further damage to a chair that had already developed a punctured tyre.

If any further damage has occurred to his power wheelchair as a result of being left with no accessible transport option after repeatedly attempting to obtain assistance, this matter will be taken further.

This was not an inconvenience. This was a person with a significant physical disability being left stranded in the Adelaide CBD for hours because an accessible transport service could not provide the service it exists to provide.

The lack of urgency, communication, professionalism and compassion throughout this entire situation was completely unacceptable.

Access Cabs needs to seriously review how this situation was handled and explain how this is considered an acceptable standard of service.
Rudest driver I have ever met. Disrespectful and condescending. Do not recommend this company to anyone. Driver of Taxi 4066 Should be ashamed.

I honestly cannot remember the last time I experienced such an unacceptable level of customer service.

The communication is absolutely appalling. When you can actually get a response, you are met with communication that comes across as rude, arrogant, dismissive and completely lacking in professionalism. Getting a straight answer seems almost impossible, and instead of being kept informed, you are left chasing, waiting and wondering what is actually happening with something you have already paid for.

The most outrageous part of my experience was the six-month wait after the product had already been paid for. Six months. That is an absolutely ridiculous amount of time to be left waiting, particularly when communication throughout the process is so poor.

There were also issues with the product being withheld, which only added to an already incredibly frustrating situation. As a paying customer, I should not have to repeatedly chase a business for a product I have already paid for, nor should I have to fight to get basic information about when I can expect to receive it.

What makes the entire situation even worse is the complete lack of accountability. Mistakes and delays can happen in any business, but what matters is how they are handled. In my experience, there was very little ownership, very little urgency and seemingly no genuine understanding of how frustrating this situation was from the customer’s perspective.

The attitude I experienced was honestly shocking. Customers deserve basic respect, transparency and communication. None of those things should be considered too much to ask.

After waiting six months for a paid product, dealing with extremely poor communication, having the product withheld and feeling like accountability was continually avoided, I have absolutely no confidence in recommending this business.

If customer service, communication and accountability matter to you, I would think very carefully before dealing with this business.

"I am writing this review with an absolutely broken heart to warn other grieving families about the devastating failure of care, hidden details, and thoughtless communication we experienced from Seasons Funerals, Redcliffe.

After the tragic loss of my 33 year old son, Myles Dixon I discovered they intended to use a basic rectangle, cardboard box for him without disclosing this to me up front. It was only after intensely questioning about the coffin that the truth came out, and I completely refused to go ahead with it. Following that I was misled into believing I had to forgo a funeral service as a trade off for a wooden coffin and my package would then only allow me to have what is termed as ' A NO ATTENDANCE, NO SERVICE CREMATION' I later discovered this was not true and both a funeral service and cremation with a veneer coffin were covered by my package. Disgraceful conduct at best by Seasons Funerals, Redcliffe!

After that deception was achieved, I was explicitly promised by our arranger, Lea, Pedelty that a coffin would be used and as I  was not permitted to attend, nobody was, I would be kept informed when Myles was leaving for the crematorium at and that photos of the finalized coffin would be sent to me beforehand. I held onto that promise so that on receiving that call, I could mentally and emotionally prepare myself for that final moment. Instead, they broke their word and sent nothing.

At 1:45 pm on the cremation day, Wednesday, September 30,  while still waiting for my call, completely out of the blue, an automated computer notification from the Metropolitan Cemeteries Board dropped into my inbox informing me that the cremation was already finished and that my son's ashes were ready for collection. The sudden, cold shock of finding out through a system-generated email tore through me like a physical blow, causing me to collapse on my lounge floor in a state of raw trauma.

I emailed Lea over 24 hours later expressing my profound hurt, and true to their ongoing lack of care, I received absolutely no answer. Seasons Funerals completely stole my final moment of closure—a sacred moment I can never get back. To make a grieving mother and brother feel completely invisible and secondary at the absolute lowest point of our lives is unforgivable. Their negligence has made our deep grief infinitely harder to bear. If you expect transparency, a gentle touch, and basic human empathy during your darkest hour, please go elsewhere. Then the deception from Seasons Funerals only continued to grow more calculated. After being completely ignored for another 24 hours by Lea, I finally bypassed her and sent a formal complaint straight to their Head Office. Exactly 30 minutes later a curt email from Lea popped into my inbox. She actively ignored my request to provide a copy of our signed contract, which is a legal requirement and also holds the written coffin conditions.

Instead, she attached three 'proof' photographs of a  standard veneer coffin as evidence that a cardboard box was not used as they had originally planned. I have now forensically exposed these coffin photos as completely fabricated. All digital camera metadata and timestamps were intentionally deleted from the files to hide when they were taken. Two different shaped coffins were used in the first and second photographs and in the second the nameplate magically moves to a completely different location proving they were manually shifting loose plaques around on showroom display models two days after my son was cremated just to snap fake angles to cover their tracks. The three name plates are not metal, as promised and all are of difference appearance and look like something hastily printed off from a laptop at the last  minute.

THE MISLEADING BEHAVIOUR AND DECEPTIVE ACTIONS FROM ALL INVOLVED AT SEASONS FUNERALS AND THE OUTRIGHT DENIALS AND GASLIGHTING I HAVE BEEN SUBJECTED TO, HAVE TURNED OUR FAMILY'S DEVASTATING LOSS OF OUR MUCH LOVED SON AND BROTHER INTO A CATASTROPHIC NIGHTMARE.  I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS BUSINESS TO ANYONE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.

Really disappointing and baffling experience this morning.

Supercheap Auto tested our battery and confirmed it was low. My husband then asked them to supply and install a replacement, but they refused because the removable bonnet prop had been sitting inside the passenger side of the car when we arrived.

We'd had to jump-start the car that morning and, in the rush, my husband had removed the prop and put it in the car. At Supercheap he simply put it straight back into its normal position and used it to support the bonnet.

We were then told that because the prop wasn't already in place when we arrived, they considered the bonnet unsafe and wouldn't install the battery. Mind you that had just tested the battery and had no issue with the bonnet then 🤦‍♀️

I've attached photos taken immediately afterwards. The prop is intact, fitted into its mounting point and was securely holding the bonnet open. The bonnet then remained open like this for approximately 20 minutes while I drove there to jump-start the car yet again.

What made the experience considerably worse was the way the situation was handled. When I spoke to the manager, I found her incredibly combative rather than interested in trying to help us find a solution. At one point, out of frustration, I said to her, "Look, you could just be a human and be helpful.” Her response was that "there are lines I can't cross."

I completely understand that businesses have safety policies and that staff shouldn't be expected to do something they genuinely believe is dangerous. But there is also a way to communicate with and help a customer who is standing there with a car that won't start. We weren't asking anyone to ignore an obviously dangerous situation. In the end, we had to jump-start the car again and went to a local battery business instead. They had no issue with the bonnet, happily supplied and installed the battery, and charged us less than Supercheap Auto would have.

So instead of getting our business that day and potentially in the future, Supercheap lost it altogether.

I understand having safety procedures. What I don't understand is applying them without any common sense or compassion, and then being combative with a customer who is simply asking for help.

I know reviews probably don’t make much of a difference for a post office, and I very rarely leave reviews—especially one-star reviews—but my experience was so genuinely awful that I felt I had to say something.
I visited to return a package for the first time and asked what I thought was a very simple question about how the process worked. Instead of receiving basic guidance, I was met with an attitude that was rude, dismissive, and incredibly condescending. From the moment I asked my question, I was made to feel like I was an inconvenience simply for not already knowing the process.
Everyone has to return a package for the first time at some point. I wasn’t making a complaint, arguing, or expecting anyone to do everything for me—I was simply asking for help so I could do it correctly. Instead, I left feeling embarrassed and genuinely shocked by the way I was spoken to.
I completely understand that customer service can be stressful and that people have bad days. That’s why I don’t complain lightly. But there is a line between being busy and treating someone with basic courtesy, and unfortunately that line was crossed today. The level of disrespect I experienced over such a simple question was completely unnecessary.
What disappointed me most is that the entire interaction could have been resolved with a polite explanation that would have taken no extra effort. Instead, I was made to feel belittled for asking a perfectly reasonable question. Interestingly, the staff member’s attitude changed noticeably by the end of the transaction, which only made the interaction at the beginning feel even more unnecessary.
I left feeling genuinely upset by the experience. It wasn’t just poor customer service—it was one of the most disrespectful interactions I’ve had while simply trying to access a basic service. I hope no one else, especially someone unfamiliar with the process, is made to feel the way I did.

We had a visit from two members of your staff today at approximately 2:55pm.

While we are always very happy to welcome and assist genuine customers, today’s visit became both uncomfortable and unnecessarily demanding.

We were subjected to what felt like around 50 questions regarding our products, where and how we source our stock, our suppliers and various other aspects of our business. This went well beyond normal customer enquiries and took a considerable amount of our staff’s time during trading hours.

We also did not appreciate some of the unsolicited comments made about our stock. Every retailer has its own buying philosophy, clientele and product selection, and commentary of this nature is neither necessary nor particularly courteous when visiting another business.

On leaving, your staff then commented that they had received “bad customer service”.

Having operated our business for 25 years, we have a very clear understanding of customer service and take considerable pride in the service we provide. Good customer service, however, does not require a retailer to answer an unlimited number of questions about its sourcing, suppliers and business practices, nor to accept inappropriate commentary about its merchandise.

Perhaps most concerning is that both individuals were wearing their employer’s uniform while conducting themselves in this manner. When representing an employer so visibly, comments and behaviour inevitably reflect upon that business.

We are always pleased to assist genuine customers and extend professional courtesy to others in our industry. We simply expect the same courtesy in return.

This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had.

I purchased a TV from Harvey Norman and trusted that I would receive a brand-new product in perfect condition. Instead, the TV was delivered damaged and broken. I reported the problem immediately, expecting Harvey Norman to take responsibility and provide a reasonable solution.

Instead of resolving the issue, they rejected my claim and accused me of damaging the TV myself during installation. I completely disagree with this. The TV was delivered to me damaged, yet somehow I am the one being blamed and left with a broken TV that I paid full price for.

As the retailer that sold and supplied the TV to me, I expected Harvey Norman to stand behind the product they delivered and properly address my complaint—not simply shift the blame onto the customer.

I have wasted my time and energy trying to resolve a problem that should never have been mine in the first place. Receiving a damaged TV is already unacceptable, but then being accused of causing the damage myself made the experience even worse.

Based on my personal experience, I would NEVER purchase from Harvey Norman again, and I cannot recommend them to anyone. I strongly recommend considering other retailers where you may receive better customer service and support if something goes wrong.

If you still decide to purchase an expensive item from Harvey Norman, I strongly suggest recording the delivery and the entire unboxing process from start to finish, because if your product arrives damaged, you may find yourself having to prove that you didn’t cause it.

Extremely disappointing and unacceptable. I expected far better from a major Australian retailer. I will take my business elsewhere in the future.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am sharing my experience to warn others about the administrative and financial practices at this clinic. I recently had an issue where an insurer sent a duplicate rebate payment to the clinic. Despite the clinic receiving these funds on the 23rd, I was not informed, even when I visited in person on the 26th. I only discovered the payment had been received after I took the initiative to call my insurer myself.
When I raised the issue, the clinic refused to refund the money, claiming that because the initial error was "not their fault," they were not obligated to issue a refund. They attempted to force me to keep the funds as a credit for future sessions, effectively holding my money hostage to ensure I continued my appointments.
It is important to note that a business has a professional and ethical obligation to return funds that do not belong to them, regardless of who caused the initial payment error. The clinic's argument that they don't have to refund me because they didn't "make the mistake" is an attempt to shirk their responsibility as the custodian of my funds.
Furthermore, I was told that the work required to reconcile these payments was a "waste of their time." This is a blatant double standard; the clinic is highly proactive and persistent when chasing clients for payments, yet characterizes the basic professional duty of fixing their own billing discrepancies as a "burden."
I have spent a significant amount of my own time acting as a debt collector for the clinic just to retrieve my own money. This lack of transparency, combined with the refusal to provide a simple refund, has made me feel completely uncomfortable continuing my care here. I would strongly advise others to be very cautious regarding their billing practices.

Hi Laura, my review is fair. U were the only one kept complaining about wasting ur time and claimed ‘not ur fault’ when things happened. Well it’s not ur fault, do u think u have the right to hold the money for the service didn’t provide yet?

I spent a day go over and over with u. It’s nothing about whose fault is, u been giving me attitude the entire time. If simply asking u to obtain ur duty is given u more burden. I suggested u to reconsider of having this job.

STOP SAYING IT’S UNFAIR, U DESERVED THIS!!

It is highly concerning that this business operates under a double standard. The owner has explicitly stated in their own correspondence that they have the right to argue that their time was wasted due to an administrative error. Yet, when I share my own experience regarding the poor service and hostile attitude I received, they label my review 'unfair' and publicly accuse me of 'intentional harm'. My distress and the impact on my mental health are just as valid as any inconvenience they claim to have experienced. I am a client who was treated with unprofessionalism, and I have every right to document that reality. Attempting to silence a client's feedback while claiming your own grievances are valid is not the behavior of a professional business.

UPDATE – 30 September 2026: I have revised this review following formal legal correspondence directly from the firm’s principal (Tony Separovic) asserting that aspects of my original review were defamatory & demanding it's immediate removal under threat of legal action. The firm stated that I could provide a revised review confined strictly to my personal experience. I have therefore revised my review accordingly based on documented facts.

**Very disappointing client intake experience**

I received a call from the firm at 9:18 AM which lasted approx. 50 minutes. I was dealing with an active wrist injury & was asked detailed questions about my personal circumstances, employment, medical history & claim. During the call, Kenzo told me that he was based in the Philippines.
During the call, I said I was uncomfortable with the lengthy questioning & asked whether the questions could instead be sent to me by email, but I was asked to remain on the call so the info could be provided to the lawyer.
At the end of the call, I was told that an appointment with a lawyer was being arranged for Wednesday at 2:00 PM. However, at 12:05 PM that same day, I received an email from Kenzo advising that the firm was unable to assist me “given the current high caseload of claims in the practice.”

I found this experience extremely disappointing. In my view, spending approx. 50 minutes going through a detailed intake process while injured, after I had asked to provide the info. by email, only to have the matter declined less than two hours later because of the firm's current high caseload, was an unnecessary waste of my time. I was particularly disappointed to be told that an appointment with a lawyer was being arranged, only to receive the rejection shortly afterwards.

Unfortunately, my experience with CV People Australia was almost the complete opposite of the process they advertise on their website.

I paid almost $900 for a professionally written, bespoke, ATS-ready CV. Their website says resumes are written from scratch with no templates, no AI and no content recycled from other clients. It also talks about clear turnaround times, confidentiality and ongoing support, yet in my experience? almost none of that happened...

Communication was poor and deadlines were missed. The CV I received was heavily templated and AI-generated, despite their explicit statements that they do not use AI or templates. When I raised my concerns, they admitted a template had been used!

The service was also sold as being ATS-ready, however the layout, formatting and the use of text boxes actually created ATS compatibility issues. For a professional CV service, this was really concerning.

MOST seriously... the first draft I received contained another client’s career information, referencing mining experience in the Middle East and Africa. Given their website states that engagements are strictly confidential and that content is not recycled between clients, I found this extremely concerning.

I gave them repeated opportunities to rectify the issues and went through three rounds of revisions, providing detailed feedback each time.

What disappointed me most was the lack of acknowledgement or meaningful support when I raised these concerns. I wasn’t expecting perfection on a first draft, but I did expect the service and process I paid for to broadly resemble what was advertised.

After multiple attempts to resolve the issues, I ultimately requested a full refund, for which I've had no response to, so instead I have now had to involved my bank seeking compensation.

Based on my experience, I wouldn't recommend CV People Australia and suggest you avoid their service entirely.

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience at Perth Steamworks on Friday night.

I’ve been a regular at Steamworks for some time and have always enjoyed the atmosphere and the overall vibe of the venue. I’ve never previously had my bag checked, although I completely understand that staff have the right to request a bag check and I have no issue with that. Because it had never been an issue previously, it honestly never crossed my mind that I might still have something private in my handbag that I had forgotten was there.

When I arrived on Friday, staff noticed a small black case inside my handbag. I genuinely didn’t realise it was still in there. It contained something personal that I wasn’t comfortable showing to security, which I explained.

I was more than willing to resolve the situation. I offered to take the item straight back to my car and then return to the venue. I wasn’t trying to bring a prohibited item inside, I wasn’t refusing to remove it from the premises, and I was offering what I thought was a very simple and reasonable solution.

Instead, I was refused entry altogether. When I asked if I could either take the item to my car and return or receive my money back, I was still told I couldn’t come back in.

What made the situation considerably worse was the attitude of the staff. The first staff member I was dealing with simply put his hand up, told me no, and walked away. Another staff member then took over and insisted that they needed to see what was inside the case. When I explained that it was a private item and that I wasn’t comfortable showing it to them, the response came across as unnecessarily sarcastic and patronising.

I completely understand that Steamworks has security policies and conditions of entry. I respect the fact that staff have a job to do and that they are entitled to enforce those policies. What I don’t understand is why, when I had immediately offered to remove the item from the venue and leave it in my car, there couldn’t have been a little more discretion or basic customer service.

Nobody even knew what was inside the case. They only knew that it was a small black case. I was offering to remove it rather than trying to sneak it into the venue.

What is particularly disappointing is that this experience felt very different from the Steamworks I have previously known. I have always considered Steamworks to have a welcoming and enjoyable atmosphere, but the attitude of some of the newer staff has unfortunately made the experience feel unpleasantly unwelcoming.

As a regular customer, that’s disappointing. Security is important, but so is the way customers are spoken to and treated. There is a huge difference between enforcing a venue policy professionally and making a paying customer feel embarrassed, dismissed and unwelcome.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and looks at how situations like this are handled, because I would hate to see the atmosphere and sense of community that has made Steamworks a place I’ve regularly enjoyed being eroded by poor customer service.

**FORMAL COMPLAINT – WASHING MACHINE HOT WATER FAILURE AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSE**

I am writing to formally raise a serious concern regarding the large washing machine and its advertised hot-water function.

I contacted management to report that the washing machine did not appear to be operating with hot water. Following my complaint, a cleaner attended and checked the water supply pipe and advised that hot water was available from the pipe.

However, this does not establish that the washing machine itself is correctly receiving, heating or using hot water during its wash cycle.

I remained present during the wash and personally checked the external glass of the machine. Throughout the cycle, it remained cold and there was no apparent indication that the selected hot-water function was operating as expected.

I raised this concern with management and requested that the machine be properly investigated. I was advised that nothing further could be done because hot water was apparently available. To my knowledge, no qualified technician was arranged to inspect the washing machine itself or verify that its hot-water function was operating correctly.

This response is particularly concerning because customers are paying to use a machine with a hot-water option and should reasonably expect that function to operate as represented.

I also informed the cleaner that I had experienced itching and skin irritation following use of the washing machine. I am not making a medical determination as to the cause; however, given the circumstances, I believe my complaint warranted proper investigation rather than simply checking whether hot water was present at the supply pipe.

I have health and safety qualifications and take matters involving customer safety seriously. In my view, once management has been put on notice of a potential equipment or safety issue, the appropriate response is to properly investigate the reported problem and, where necessary, arrange for a competent technician to inspect the equipment.

Please treat this correspondence as a **formal written complaint and notice of the reported issue**. I recommend that management retain a record of this complaint and arrange for the machine to be professionally inspected, including verification of the actual water temperature during the relevant wash cycle.

If another customer experiences the same issue and requires a witness regarding the condition of the machine or the fact that this concern was previously raised with management, I am prepared to provide an account of what I personally observed and reported.

I reserve my right to raise the matter with the appropriate consumer protection, health and safety, or other relevant authority if the issue remains unresolved.

I am disappointed that, despite bringing the matter directly to management's attention, the response was simply that nothing further could be done without arranging a technical inspection of the machine.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with our experience with Fertility One. I was clear from the beginning that I was seeking further investigation following recurrent miscarriages and wanted to explore natural/less invasive options before considering IVF. They confirmed they could assist us and arranged a consultation with a doctor they advised was appropriate for our circumstances.

Before our initial consultation, I contacted the clinic to confirm they had received all the tests and information required and was told they had. This was also confirmed during our consultation. However, during the consultation, I felt that the focus was primarily on me rather than on us as a couple, including my partner's relevant history and investigations. It also did not appear that our file and test results had been thoroughly reviewed before the appointment. There was little discussion about further testing to investigate the possible reasons for our recurrent miscarriages.

More concerningly, the consultation proceeded without the clinic having received many of the tests they subsequently advised were mandatory for the consultation. We only discovered this when I requested our results because I felt we had not been provided with enough information. I was initially told that I had not completed the testing, but after contacting the pathology provider myself, I was advised that the tests needed to be repeated. Pathology advised that the doctor ordering the tests should have informed us of this. I was then told Fertility One would normally follow up missing results for patients undergoing treatment, but as I wasn't proceeding with current treatment, this had not occurred. I therefore had to arrange the repeat testing and follow up myself, including through my GP.

After seeking another fertility opinion, we identified additional factors that could have been relevant to our fertility journey, including standard investigations that are not unusual when assessing recurrent miscarriages or considering IVF. In my view, these should have at least been discussed given our history and the reason we were seeking specialist advice.

I was also sent a tax invoice for services/treatments that were not related to my case or file, which added to my concerns about the accuracy and administration of our records.

Missing test results may sound like an administrative issue, but for us they were potentially much more significant. We were looking for answers following recurrent miscarriages, and those tests could potentially have identified a reason for our losses. Missing relevant results could mean an underlying issue is overlooked and potentially contribute to another miscarriage without us knowing that something important had been missed.

If a clinic can miss multiple results, including tests they say are mandatory for their consultation, and proceed with the appointment without identifying this, it raises a genuine concern about what other important information may potentially be overlooked in a patient's file.

My concern is not that fertility treatment cannot guarantee an outcome. It is the lack of communication, attention to detail, follow up and accountability. We ultimately felt more like a number than patients receiving personalised care, particularly when we were not immediately proceeding with IVF.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend Fertility One to someone seeking thorough investigation and personalised care before deciding whether IVF is right for them.

one_star_reviews.text:
Smith Lawyers were our first choice to represent us in what we were repeatedly told was a strong case. We placed our trust in the firm and believed they would stand by us throughout the process. Unfortunately, after approximately 10 months, and after numerous lawyers and paralegals were dismissed or left the firm, Smith Lawyers ultimately decided to discontinue acting for us.

What made this particularly devastating was that, throughout those 10 months, we were repeatedly told by lawyers at Smith Lawyers that we had a strong case. We invested an enormous amount of time, energy and emotional strength into the process, only to find ourselves back at the beginning with no legal representation and no realistic way of continuing.

The consequences of what happened to us have been life-altering. We lost approximately $30,000 worth of personal belongings as a result of the events surrounding the property and were left dealing with PTSD, FND and other significant mental-health difficulties. At the same time, we were struggling financially and facing the very real possibility of homelessness.

The PIPA claim involved Landlink Realty and the property owners, Robyn and Robert Ryan. Despite everything we had endured, we ultimately had to give up pursuing the claim because we could not find another law firm willing or able to represent us. Continuing to retell what happened became increasingly harmful. Each time we had to revisit the events, we were forced to relive an experience that had already changed our lives.

We also found the interactions surrounding the matter extremely distressing, particularly the treatment and responses we experienced from Rob and Lachlan Boyle. We felt that we were repeatedly placed in a position where we had to defend ourselves and our experiences while already dealing with significant psychological and physical consequences.

Losing our belongings, our financial security and our sense of stability, while developing significant mental-health difficulties following an event that fundamentally changed our lives, was horrendous. Having to look directly at the possibility of homelessness while simultaneously trying to cope with PTSD, FND and the emotional consequences of everything that had happened was overwhelming.

Ultimately, we did not give up because we believed what happened to us was insignificant. We gave up because we had exhausted our options, could not secure legal representation and were emotionally and financially unable to keep putting ourselves through the process. After everything we had already endured, continuing to rehash the events without any realistic prospect of representation became too damaging.

We found out that "downsizing" happens yearly at Smith Lawyers unfortunately we were one of the people who copped the brunt of it and had to walk away with nothing at all.

I’m extremely disappointed with the way my TPD claim has been handled. It has now been months, and I have completed everything that was asked of me, including attending medical appointments with the doctor.

I was told that the preliminary assessment form had been paid, and that was over a month ago. Since then, I have tried contacting them several times but received no response. I eventually received a call and was told that the reason it was taking so long was because the preliminary form had not actually been paid for

At this point, I’m extremely frustrated and concerned because I have been given conflicting information. Someone is clearly not providing me with accurate information, and this whole situation has caused me unnecessary stress that I simply don’t need.

I understand that claims can take time, but clear communication and honesty are extremely important when dealing with something as serious as a TPD claim. After doing everything that was asked of me, I expected much better communication and professionalism.

one_star_reviews.text:
Patient safety rhetoric rings hollow when basic standards of care are neglected

My experience raises serious concerns about this facility’s priorities, particularly the apparent disconnect between its stated commitment to patient safety and the standard of care and communication actually experienced.

Communication between clinical staff, patients and families is frequently inadequate. Some staff members appear to have limited English proficiency, creating persistent communication barriers that make it difficult to exchange information, clarify clinical matters and ensure that patients and their families are properly informed. This is not a trivial inconvenience. Effective communication is a fundamental component of patient safety, continuity of care and informed decision-making. Rather than addressing these basic requirements, the facility seems content to operate despite recurring communication difficulties.

The advertised amenities and specialist services, including the gym and movie theatre, also appear to be unavailable in practice. Promoting services that patients cannot reliably access creates expectations that the facility subsequently fails to meet, further undermining confidence in its overall offering.

Perhaps most frustrating is the apparent prioritisation of restrictive infection-control procedures over more immediate and tangible aspects of patient care. Patients and visitors are subjected to rapid antigen testing upon entry and required to wait outside in freezing conditions. The proportionality and practical justification of these arrangements deserve scrutiny, particularly when the burdens imposed on patients and families are considered alongside the actual benefits of the measures. Infection prevention is important, but policies should be evidence-informed, proportionate, regularly reviewed and implemented with due consideration for patient dignity and comfort.

Similarly, vaccination requirements during flu season raise legitimate questions about the distinction between reducing the risk of severe disease and meaningfully preventing transmission. These are not interchangeable outcomes. Infection-control policies should be justified by transparent evidence, clearly communicated objectives and a demonstrated relationship to patient safety, rather than treated as inherently effective simply because they are restrictive.

And this brings me to the facility’s apparent mantra: “Our first priority is our patients.”

That statement is difficult to take seriously when basic communication problems persist, advertised services are unavailable and patients and their families are subjected to burdensome procedures without an adequately demonstrated consideration of their practical impact.

If patient safety is genuinely the first priority, why isn’t there an equally visible commitment to ensuring that clinical staff can communicate effectively with patients and families? Why are fundamental aspects of the patient experience seemingly neglected while administrative compliance and restrictive entry procedures receive such attention?

Patient safety is not synonymous with imposing the greatest possible number of restrictions. It requires sound clinical judgement, competent communication, proportionate risk management and a consistent focus on the actual needs of patients.

A facility cannot credibly claim that patients come first while overlooking the very fundamentals that make patients safe, informed and properly cared for. Until its operational priorities align with its stated values, the slogan “Our first priority is our patients” comes across as little more than corporate rhetoric.

Don’t bother looking me up and then trivialise this review by the classic corporate “we acknowledge your concerns but can’t find you on the system.”

My experience with the behaviour specialist from Ability Action was absolutely appalling. I would give zero stars if Google allowed it.
The level of professionalism, communication and genuine understanding of the participant’s needs was far below what I would expect from someone working with vulnerable people in the disability sector.
What was most concerning was the complete lack of confidence I was left with in the service being provided. Behaviour support is an area where competence, communication, accountability and collaboration with the participant’s support network are critical. In my experience, those standards were simply not met.
Dealing with the situation became unnecessarily frustrating and stressful, and I was extremely disappointed with the way matters were handled.
When families and providers engage a behaviour specialist, they are placing an enormous amount of trust in that person. They deserve someone who listens, communicates clearly, works collaboratively and puts the participant at the centre of every decision.
Based on my experience, I could not recommend Ability Action's behaviour support service and would strongly encourage anyone considering them to ask detailed questions about the practitioner assigned to them, their experience, communication practices and approach before proceeding.

Had one of the worst experiences at Parramatta Motor Group, Camellia. I am quite dissatisfied with team.
I arrived at 8:30 AM for my car service, expecting it to be completed within a reasonable timeframe. However, by 1:30 PM, the mechanics had still not completed the service. The tyres were also not changed.
When I followed up, I was given excuses about staff shortages and staff being on breaks, rather than receiving clear communication about the delay or a reasonable solution.
If there was a staffing issue, this should have been communicated to customers upfront instead of leaving them waiting for hours without proper updates.
Overall, I found the experience extremely frustrating and disappointing. The communication was poor, the service was unnecessarily delayed, and the customer service did not meet expectations. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and improves the way customers are treated and kept informed.

Sahara Solar installed our solar system in 2022, so I thought I was giving my deposit to a trustworthy company when I paid a 50% deposit in August 2025 for a home battery.

Unfortunately, my experience with Sahara Solar this time has been terrible. Their complete incompetence and utter disregard for returning customers are now on clear display.

Their excuses for delays include installers resigning at short notice and personal problems - in all of these instances, the company should have been upfront and returned my deposit if they were unable to provide the contracted service.

After six months of promises of "asap" and "thanks for your patience", I cancelled the order given their track record of poor communication, failure to provide the system in a reasonable time-fame, and lack of confidence that they could provide any after sales support.

The manager initially told me I would get my deposit back in five working days. It has now been a further six months I am still trying to get my deposit back. I agreed to a payment plan after the New Energy Tech Consumer Code (NETCC) involvement - however Sahara Solar did not make any of the payments and are not responding to my emails.

I've been through Consumer Affairs Victoria, and the NETCC who have expelled them from the NETCC program. And I have an ongoing case with VCAT. It also appears that their ABN has been cancelled.

It's unclear if the business is still operational or if they have gone bust. Read recent reviews on Google and solar quotes and avoid this company at all cost.

I was told to see a psychologist after trying to report being the victim of abuse. When I was suffering and distressed by my compromised situation, I experienced the psychologist as treating me as an inconvenience, cold, judgemental, unsympathetic, not able to understand my experiences (such as distress invalidation from the legal system had caused me), or comprehend the abusive situations I was in (such as experiencing bullying from my workplace boss), forgetful of who I was (after I already attended multiple times asked me “have you been here before?”) and demonstrating inappropriate irritation toward me in the form of shouting - using my session time which was supposed to help me “recover from abuse” to literally shout at me repeatedly.

When I tried to communicate I didn’t find the psychologist helpful, she barked “personality disorder” at me in a derogatory way. I have since been diagnosed with CPTSD and informed BPD is a pejorative term and a misdiagnosis.

When I tried to report my experience to AHPRA she denied it, which was further mentally damaging.

I am writing this because I was naive and too trusting and wish I was better informed so I could decline to see psychologists even though they kept being pushed on me, and advocate for my funding to go towards things that would actually help me.

I didn’t trust the experience to go well as I’ve actually had a really awful experience here a few times, and with the sales assistant in particular, so I recorded the conversation on my watch. My mum had a really awful experience with her this afternoon, and all she wanted was to refund a bag, that she didn’t get a tax invoice with through an online order.

The sales assistant was accusing me of harassing her, yelling at her, making her feel unsafe, video recording her, and saying that she doesn’t want to serve me. She was saying all of this over the phone to I’m unsure who she was speaking to at the time, but it was done on the shop floor, which I find quite unprofessional and uncomfortable for myself, especially as I’ve worked in retail most of my life and was a store manager, so I know how awful it can feel when a customer is rude to you. Yet not once in the voice recording could you hear me raise my voice, yell at her, make her feel uncomfortable or anything, even when she was raising her voice at me. She was raising her voice at me which I’ve got on the recording and was saying “what do you want me to do, what would you want me to do?” “You not having a receipt is not my concern” “I can’t do anything for you”.

She spoke to someone else when I originally came in, which I knew was about my mum, saying that the girl at midland (who she mentioned by the name of Caitlin?) told her the online refund couldn’t be done in store, and that the regional manager Dave said the same thing; that it couldn’t be done. She told me that she couldn’t refund things from the online store and purchases from other stores made outside of Morley; to which I told her she’d previously sent me back to Karrinyup to refund a suitcase I bought that was broken and then she said she’s never had problems refunding from other stores so it was a problem with my order. Contradicting herself entirely, which the girls at Karrinyup said was incorrect and it could have been refunded at Morley to save myself driving 30 minutes to Karrinyup. Even though Caitlin who was actually really nice and lovely over the phone was able to walk her through the process of finding the order on the system and refunding it in the end.

My mum is usually someone who’s not shaken easily, but she was left in tears when I got home from work. Imagine being called a thief, told to “get the hell out of here”, and accused of taking photos of her. All while my mum gave her, her own phone which she went through to see my mum didn’t take photos of her.

I wouldn’t recommend this store; as I’ve also walked in here previously and have been ignored, treated unkindly, and turned away from receiving help.

I’ll gladly travel further to Karrinyup or Midland, just to avoid ever feeling the way I’m made to feel at this store.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely Disgraceful Customer Service
I would give QBE zero stars if I could.

I have been paying approximately $4,000 a year for my insurance, and after being involved in an accident that was not my fault, I expected my insurer to actually support me. Instead, I have spent an exhausting amount of time being passed between approximately 10 different people, repeatedly explaining the same situation and receiving little to no meaningful assistance.

My experience with Franch from Dispute Resolution, working under Marty O'Donoghue, was particularly appalling.

Her attitude was extremely dismissive, rude and condescending. Rather than attempting to understand my concerns or provide a solution, I was essentially told:

“This is not my claim, this is not my complaint. You can go ahead and deal and contact the third party who hit your car yourself.”»

Seriously — what exactly am I paying $4,000 a year for?

If I have to chase the third party myself after an accident that wasn't my fault, why am I paying QBE thousands of dollars for insurance?

The complete lack of empathy and willingness to assist was shocking. I was not treated like a customer who had paid for a service; I was treated like a problem that needed to be passed elsewhere.

And calling someone a “Dispute Resolution Specialist” creates an expectation that they will actually help resolve disputes. Unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite. I received no meaningful resolution, no reassurance and no sense that my concerns were being taken seriously.

This was one of the worst customer-service experiences I have ever had.

QBE should seriously reconsider how its dispute-resolution team handles customers. People dealing with the aftermath of an accident need professionalism, empathy, respect and solutions — not attitude, dismissal and instructions to handle everything themselves.

I have paid QBE thousands of dollars for peace of mind. Instead, when I actually needed help, I was left feeling completely abandoned.

QBE has seriously damaged my trust in the company, and based on this experience, I would NOT recommend QBE to anyone looking for an insurer that will genuinely stand behind its customers when they need it most.

one_star_reviews.text:
BUYER BEWARE – FOUR DRESSES, FOUR QUALITY FAILURES

Sadly, my experience with Natasha Gan has been terrible. What started as purchasing a dress in June for an August wedding turned into months of replacements, repeated defects and unnecessary stress. After receiving four dresses, I still did not have a dress I could confidently wear to the wedding.

Dress 1: For the price, I was shocked to discover the dress was polyester. I accept that I should have checked the fabric composition before purchasing, but at this price point I simply didn't expect it. The dress also had a flower incorrectly stitched over another area and persistent creasing that I could not iron out.

Dress 2: The placement of the print left a large black gap directly at the front of the dress, which looked terrible. I contacted Natasha Gan and was advised they couldn't control where the print was positioned, but they agreed to provide another replacement.

Dress 3: This was where things became unbelievable. The dress arrived with numerous flowers missing from the embroidery and, in their place, there were what appeared to be numbers/markings stitched into the fabric. At this point I requested a refund. I was advised that a refund would not be provided and that I would have to accept another replacement.

I reluctantly agreed.

Dress 4: Honestly, by this stage I didn't know whether to laugh or cry. The fourth dress arrived with pockets at noticeably different heights, a hole in a pocket, further missing flowers and more of the strange stitched numbers/markings throughout the dress.

I had been assured each time that the replacement dresses would be inspected before being sent. Looking at what I received, I genuinely cannot understand how these obvious defects could have passed any reasonable quality-control inspection.

I emailed again with photographs and explained the stress this ongoing situation had caused. I originally purchased the dress in June specifically for an August wedding. After four dresses, I was running out of time and still had nothing suitable to wear. I am certainly not in a position to simply keep spending money on dresses, so I needed the refund to purchase something else at short notice.

The designs may photograph beautifully, but based on my experience there appears to be a serious lack of quality control, and the way my repeated problems were handled left me extremely disappointed.

I also paid through PayPal believing I had additional buyer protection, but by the time the problems continued through to the third replacement, I discovered I was unable to lodge the dispute I had expected to be able to make.

I believe people need to be aware of the quality issues with Natasha Gan before you spend $350 on a dress. Four dresses with significant quality issues is not an isolated manufacturing fault.

I rarely leave reviews like this, but other customers deserve to know what my experience has been before spending their money.

Sadly, I would never recommend Natasha Gan. Buyer beware.

My wife and I first came into contact with Northern Pain Clinic with a consultation with Professor Michael Cousins. I was at that stage a physiotherapist running a clinic in Woollahra called Physioworks. Professor Cousins was in my opinion a highly regarded pain specialist, a leader in the field. He was proposing an implant to be inserted in my wife’s spine. I was familiar with the technology and was very keen for my wife to proceed. Professor Cousins detailed some cases where the recipient had greatly reduced their pain. He stated he was too old to do the actual surgery, but would oversee the post operative management. On the day of the surgery, we were surprised to find Professor Cousins intended to do the surgery. It failed to reduce any pain, and i later researched the implant to be now regarded as not as we understood it. The unit had to be removed, we were told a difficulty with it working was the amount of titanium implants. This seemed a poor excuse that could have been overcome should any preoperative scans be observed. We were made to undergo about the most absurd physiotherapy session (walk around the house) and psychology session (be positive). We left, I no longer had any regard for Professor Cousins, but didn’t think we would ever again need his services.

Fast forward an (unknown) number of years and my wife is about to become a patient at Wyvern Hospital. A hospital in which North Shore Pain Clinic is the responsible accredited pain relief specialists. Given the extensive pain history of my wife, up to her undergoing a full hospital inpatient withdrawl from her prescribed methadone, a sight no husband should observe, let alone his wife should endure. My concern at her proposed pain management strategy for the upcoming neck surgery was of TOP PRORIORITY as far as I was concerned. Understanding, and having spent 30 years corresponding with pain specialists has led to the OPINION of mine that most are not worth the phone call, let alone the trust that patients place in them, (we have found one,  but will not reveal his name). The receptionist at the North Shore Pain center was probably the rudest medical receptionist I’ve ever come across. She refused to allow me to talk to the specialist I believed would ‘look after’’ my wife. I rang, I emailed my concerns, wrote of her pain history and medications used, including Buvidal, an AI description will alert the reader to my problem ‘Buvidal acts as an opioid partial agonist-antagonist, meaning it has properties of both types of drugs depending on which receptor it targets’. I can, mostly, understand that. I hoped the pain specialist could, but needed proof. The practice and I already had ‘history’. I found out, while my wife was already in ICU at Wyvern Hospital that no pain specialist from North Shore Pain Centre would bother turning up. Luckily the ‘normal’ expert management team proved to be up to the task, and while her recovery was complex,  her pain was managed as best as it could be. I was, furious at the unprofessional, inhumane, unbelievable manner my wife was treated  I wrote a detailed Google review. It was not at all complimentary. Later, I was contacted with the request to take the feedback down, our surgeon requested it, so I immediately removed it. I did however state that unless the North Shore Pain Clinic contacted me and explained to me WHY they had refused to treat my wife, and WHY they had allowed us to continue in the belief that her pain would be treated, another review would be published. No such response has been made. That is the sole reason this review is here now.

I understand that an assessment has standards and nobody should simply be handed a pass. My issue is the overall experience and, particularly after subsequently training elsewhere, the enormous difference in the quality and effectiveness of the training.

I went to **Blue Horse Truck Driver Training** afterwards and the experience was night and day. They took the time to actually train me in a way that made things click, explain what was required and make sure I properly understood and could demonstrate it. I subsequently passed my MC assessment successfully.

That experience showed me what I believe good driver training should feel like.

I'm not leaving this review because I believe paying for training automatically entitles someone to a licence. It doesn't. I'm leaving it because when you're spending this sort of money, you expect the training to prepare you effectively for the assessment and help you understand exactly what is required.

Having now experienced two very different approaches, I know which one I would recommend.

Unfortunately, nearly $3,000 spent with Statewide ultimately left me disappointed, out of pocket and needing to go elsewhere to achieve what I originally paid to achieve.

Based on my personal experience, **I would not recommend Statewide Truck Driver Training.**

one_star_reviews.text:
My Experience with Slater and Gordon Lawyers
Be very careful if you are considering using Slater and Gordon Lawyers. Based on my own experience, I believe people need to think very carefully before trusting this firm with their legal matter.
In my experience, they took my money, did what they wanted to do, and then I felt as though they no longer cared about me or my matter. I do not feel that they properly listened to me or acted on what I was asking them to do.
One of the managers there, in my experience, does what she wants rather than listening to the client. You can explain what you want and what you believe should happen, but they will make their own decisions and do what they want to do.

When I wanted my matter taken to court, I felt that instead of properly listening to me and considering my instructions, I was told that it was no good and that I should go somewhere else and find another lawyer. To me, that is abandoning a client when they need their lawyer the most.

I believe that if a lawyer does not agree with a client's proposed course of action, they should properly explain why and provide appropriate legal advice. They should not simply dismiss the client and leave them to find another lawyer.

Once a lawyer or law firm no longer wants to represent you, it can be extremely difficult to find another lawyer willing to take over your matter. In my view, this leaves clients in a very vulnerable position.
I have also spoken with several other clients who have told me they have experienced the same or very similar problems.

They have told me that they feel they are not helped, not listened to and that the firm does not care about their concerns.
I also believe that things have been said or represented to me that are not correct, and I dispute some of the information I have been given about my matter.

I find it very sad that a law firm that people trust to represent them can leave clients feeling this way. My personal experience has left me believing that once the firm gets its money, the client can become secondary.

I am not saying that every client will have exactly the same experience as me. I am telling people what happened to me and what other clients have told me about their experiences.

I saw another obstetrician in the Glow practice throughout my pregnancy who was unavailable at the time of my birth and Dr Monika Skubisz attended instead.

When Dr Skubisz arrived in the birthing suite, she examined me and told me I was fully dilated and therefore had to start pushing. Just half an hour earlier I had been examined by the midwife and was 9cm dilated.

I was unmedicated and had no urge to push. Despite this, I was instructed to hold my breath and push which felt completely unnatural to me and I struggled with it. I was yelled at over and over again to do as instructed and hold my breath and not to breathe out while pushing. She also began threatening me saying she would take me to theatre and use forceps. Throughout all of this she made me lie on my back because SHE was more comfortable with me in that position.

After one hour and 4 minutes of coached pushing without any natural urge she essentially made me have an episiotomy and ventouse delivery. There was no medical indication for this besides ‘prolonged second stage’. My baby was never in distress. According to SA health guidelines a one hour long second stage for a first time mother is not considered prolonged and directed valsalva pushing should be avoided.

She also kept saying she thought the baby was too big for me and I should have had growth scans throughout my pregnancy. My baby turned out to be a very average newborn size and my original obstetrician did not recommend for me to have any growth scans.

I felt coerced and bullied throughout the birth and the coached pushing and episiotomy she forced me into has caused me ongoing pelvic floor issues. I would not recommend birthing with Dr Monika Skubisz. I wish every day that she had not attended my birth.

PLEASE READ THE UPDATES TO THIS REVIEW — they are important context.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this business.

For comparison, I have since found another repairer in the Beaudesert area who I found far more helpful, transparent and worth the drive.

INITIAL CONTACT:
I called to ask for a quote and an explanation of what steps would be taken to diagnose a problem with my car, as I was trying to understand the likely costs involved. During the call, I was told words to the effect of, ‘I’m not here to tell you how to fix your car… I explained that I wasn’t asking for instructions on repairing the vehicle myself; I simply wanted to understand their diagnostic process before deciding whether to proceed. I found the interaction dismissive and didn’t feel that my questions were being answered. Based on my experience with the phone call, I decided not to proceed with this business and wouldn’t personally recommend them.

UPDATE: Following this review, I received a phone call from the business regarding my review. During that call I was told that I had 48 hours to remove my review and that legal action would be taken if I did not remove it. I found the call intimidating and upsetting and was left shaking afterwards. I will not be engaging in any further telephone conversations regarding this matter and request that any further communication be made in writing

FURTHER UPDATE following the business’s response:

Their response is lengthy, so I think it is important to clarify why my one-star review remains.

I have never claimed that this business inspected, diagnosed or repaired my vehicle. They didn’t. My review relates entirely to my experience communicating with them while I was deciding whether I wanted to engage their services.

I called because I was trying to understand what the diagnostic process would involve and what I could reasonably expect it to cost. I had already spent money trying to resolve the issue elsewhere, which is precisely why I was asking questions before committing to spending more.

The business clearly believes the original conversation should be interpreted differently. That’s their position. My experience of that conversation was that I found the manner in which my questions were answered dismissive and rude. Their response also confirms that I was ultimately told, “I’m not here to teach you how to fix it. I’m here to fix your car.” I was not asking to be taught how to repair my transmission. I was a prospective customer trying to understand what I would potentially be paying for before handing over my vehicle.

What concerns me considerably more now, however, is what happened after I left the review.

The business contacted me directly about my one-star review. During that call I was told they had listened to the original conversation, considered my review inaccurate and had spoken with their solicitor. I was told to remove the review. I refused. The call concluded with me being given 48 hours to remove it or being told they would proceed with legal action.

Yes, after being told legal action was being considered over my Google review, my responses became short and frustrated. I said words including “go for it” and ultimately “pull your head in”. I’m quite comfortable acknowledging that. I was not abusive, I did not threaten anyone, and I make no claim that I handled every second of an unexpected and confrontational phone call perfectly.

What I will not do is pretend that receiving a phone call telling me to remove a negative review within 48 hours or face legal action was an ordinary attempt to resolve an unhappy prospective customer’s experience.

I was shaking after that phone call and found the interaction extremely intimidating.

The business is entitled to disagree with my assessment of our interactions and to publish its response. Equally, I am entitled to accurately describe my own experience and explain why I chose not to become a customer.

Readers now have both accounts and can make up their own minds.

My rating remains one star…because 0 wasn’t an option!

⭐ 1 STAR — THINK TWICE BEFORE ENROLLING WITH MATRIX EDUCATION

My experience with Matrix Education has been deeply disappointing—not only academically, but also in the way my cancellation and payments have been handled.

Matrix charges premium prices, so I expected premium teaching and professional customer service. Instead, my son gained very little from the program. The tutoring did not deliver the improvement or educational value I was paying for, and in my experience, the cost was completely out of proportion to the results.

The cancellation process has been even more concerning.

I contacted Matrix more than once to cancel my son’s enrolment. Despite this, the cancellation was not properly actioned. I was then told that because an English book had been mailed for the new term, I had to physically attend a centre and return it before the cancellation could be finalised.

While this remained unresolved, more than $500 was debited from my account.

That is not a minor administrative inconvenience. It is a serious failure to handle a clear cancellation request properly. Once a parent has clearly asked to cancel, payments should not continue without transparent communication and a fair, straightforward process. If returning a book was a condition of cancellation, that should have been clearly explained when I first requested to end the enrolment—not used to justify ongoing debits afterwards.

The direct debits also occurred at times I did not expect, adding further stress and uncertainty.

When I called for help, I expected accountability and a clear resolution. Instead, I felt dismissed, ignored and passed around rather than genuinely assisted. The way this matter has been handled has left me with a complete lack of confidence in the company.

For the prices Matrix Education charges, parents should receive excellent tutoring, honest billing, clear cancellation procedures and respectful customer service. My experience fell far short on every one of those points.

Parents should be extremely cautious before enrolling and especially before authorising direct debit payments. Get every cancellation condition in writing, keep records of all communication and monitor your account closely.

I trusted Matrix Education with my son’s education and with access to my bank account. Based on my experience, I regret that decision.

The lesson I wish I had known before enrolling is simple: expensive fees do not guarantee value, and cancelling may not be as straightforward as you expect.

I would not recommend Matrix Education.

In 2024, I paid $370 for a 30 minute follow-up appointment. This service now costs $480. With how quickly this price is rising, most of us will be paying $500+ by the end of this year to see a doctor for a couple of minutes. I’m guessing that, like me, most clients are forced to pay this price to continue receiving mental health services because it would cost even more (likely thousands of dollars) to switch to a different clinic. It’s disappointing how Mind Oasis clinic seems to be taking advantage of their clients, many who are paying insane fees out of desperation so they can continue treating their mental health.

Important to note that you're required to pay $480+ each time you need to:
- contact your doctor or speak to them in any capacity
- seek advice or bring up concerns about medications
- request clarification about treatment plan
- acquire scripts for medications you have been taking for years
- request a new script if you've received an incorrect prescription

Until you and your practitioner establish a consistent treatment method, you'll be paying around $350-$500 for an appointment every three or four weeks to trial different medications and dosages. This period typically lasts 1-2 months, but it can go on indefinitely if you're resistant to most treatments and can be quite pricy as appointment fees accumulate quickly.

I do want to mention that the practitioners at Mind Oasis are wonderful (Dr. Morteza Hayati) and provide excellent care and support. My interactions with other clinic staff have also been consistently good.

But ultimately, I wouldn’t recommend Mind Oasis due to the clinic's poor management and predatory practices.

I received a phone call from one of the reception staff at around 6:30 PM on 29 September.

The caller did not introduce herself and tried to explain something to me, but due to the poor phone connection, I was unable to clearly understand what she was saying. I politely asked her to repeat the information.

To my surprise, she simply hung up the call without any explanation. When I tried calling the number back immediately, I only received an automated message saying that no one was available to take the call.

I found this experience extremely frustrating and unprofessional. Considering that this is a mental health clinic, I would expect reception staff to communicate with patients and their families with a greater level of patience, care, and professionalism.

I hope this matter can be reviewed and that staff are reminded of the importance of clear and respectful communication, particularly when dealing with people seeking mental health support.
